chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'When a man exits from his Hajj with an animal upon which a sacrificial blood (dam) is obligatory, is it sufficient for him to slaughter it when he returns to his family?' He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'As far as I know, he should give it in charity.'

Is'haq said, 'And I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'When a man exits from his Hajj with what obligates upon him the blood (dam), and he does not spill it until he returns to his family,' he said, 'He should spill it among his family, and he should eat something from it.'

key_terms.دَم: Sacrificial animal (dam) offered due to a defect or restriction in Hajj
key_terms.يَهْرِقُ: To spill blood, i.e., to slaughter

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who delays slaughtering his Hajj sacrifice until returning home?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling the dam (sacrificial animal) obligation for a pilgrim who incurs a blood liability but delays slaughter until returning home. While one view suggests donating the animal, the preferred Shia scholarly understanding, supported by the second report, permits the pilgrim to slaughter it locally and consume the meat, emphasizing practical ease. This reflects the broader juristic principle of removing hardship in Hajj rituals when specific conditions prevent immediate fulfillment.
